sections.title: Patient Positioning

sections.title: Nurse Prep Notes
sections.nurseNotes: Check scope decontamination log. Confirm fasting >6h solids / >2h clear fluids. IV access confirmed BEFORE sedation. Sedation nurse dedicated — do not leave patient unattended. Monitor SpO₂ and HR throughout. Flumazenil immediately accessible. Document all specimens with site label. If upper GI bleed: have therapeutic equipment (clips, Adrenaline 1:10,000, heater probe) ready before starting.

sections.title: Post-procedure Care
sections.recoveryNotes: Recovery in endoscopy unit until Aldrete score ≥9. Minimum 30 min observation post-sedation. No driving for 24h after sedation. Light diet when gag reflex returned if throat spray used.

sections.title: Discharge Criteria
dischargeCriteria: Written procedure report and aftercare instructions given

sections.title: Complications & Escalation
commonComplications: Perforation — senior review, surgical referral, CT confirmation
Sedation over-sedation — flumazenil, oxygen, call anaesthetics
Post-biopsy bleeding — repeat endoscopy if haemodynamically significant
Aspiration — head-down position, suction, anaesthetic support
Missed lesion — ensure adequate retroflexion and J-manoeuvre

sections.title: Nurse Prep Notes
sections.nurseNotes:
PREPARE before patient arrives: DAS difficult airway trolley checked, video laryngoscope charged and working, suction ON and at bedside, capnography ready, drugs drawn up and labelled.

DRUG SEQUENCE: Pre-oxygenation (3 min 15L NRB or 8 breaths ETOM) → Pre-treatment → Induction agent → Paralytic → Sellick's manoeuvre (cricoid) → Intubate → Confirm with capnography.

Sugammadex MUST be drawn up and labelled if rocuronium used — Cannot-Intubate-Cannot-Oxygenate rescue.

Post-intubation: secure ETT, CXR to confirm placement, commence ventilator settings.

sections.title: Complications & Escalation
commonComplications: Failed intubation — back to BVM, call for senior airway help, DAS failed intubation algorithm
Oesophageal intubation — no capnography waveform, immediate recognition and re-attempt
Hypoxia on induction — optimise pre-oxygenation, BVM support
Haemodynamic instability post-induction — ketamine preferred, push-dose adrenaline available
Bradycardia with sux in children — atropine pre-treatment

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Aseptic insertion of a urethral catheter into the male bladder for urinary drainage, urine sampling, or post-operative monitoring.
sections.anaesthesiaType: Instillagel (local anaesthetic + lubricant gel) — no sedation required

items.name: Verbal Consent
items.description: Document consent obtained and indication in nursing notes

items.name: Catheter Passport / SOP
items.description: Local policy for catheter care and documentation

items.name: Foley Catheter 14Fr
items.description: Hydrophilic coated — start with 14Fr, have 16Fr available

items.name: Urinary Drainage Bag
items.description: Standard 2L bag — or night bag as appropriate

items.name: Instillagel 11ml
items.description: Lidocaine + chlorhexidine lubricant gel — instil 3–5 min before insertion

items.name: Cleansing Swabs (×5)
items.description: Sterile swabs for meatal cleansing with saline/antiseptic

items.name: Sterile Water 10ml
items.description: Balloon inflation — use water not saline

sections.title: Nurse Prep Notes
sections.nurseNotes:
ANTT (Aseptic Non-Touch Technique) throughout — do not contaminate key parts.

INSTILLAGEL: Instil full 11ml syringe into meatus and wait 3–5 minutes before insertion — essential for comfort and tract preparation.

INSERTION: Hold penis at 90° to abdomen to straighten urethra. Advance catheter gently — do not force. If resistance at external sphincter, ask patient to breathe out and try again. Advance fully to Y-junction before inflating balloon.

BALLOON: Inflate with 10ml sterile water (NOT saline — crystallises). Patient should feel no pain on inflation — if pain, deflate immediately and advance further.

DOCUMENT: Date, time, indication, catheter size/type/batch number, balloon volume, residual on insertion, urine colour.

sections.title: Post-procedure Care
sections.recoveryNotes: Secure catheter to leg with catheter strap — prevent traction. Bag below bladder at all times — gravity drainage. Daily meatal hygiene with soap and water. Document urine output and characteristics.

sections.title: Complications & Escalation
commonComplications: Failed catheterisation — try 16Fr, consider Coudé tip catheter, refer to urology if second attempt fails
Haematuria — reassure if mild, monitor, senior review if haematuria with clots
False passage — stop immediately, urgent urology review
CAUTI (catheter-associated UTI) — remove/change catheter at 5–7 days per policy, MSU sample
Bypassing — check catheter not blocked, consider smaller catheter, bladder spasm treatment

sections.summary: Aseptic insertion of a urethral catheter into the female bladder. Shorter urethra than male — technique varies.
sections.anaesthesiaType: Lubricant gel — no local anaesthetic usually required for female catheterisation

items.name: Lubricating Gel

sections.title: Nurse Prep Notes
sections.nurseNotes: Patient in supine position, knees bent and apart. Good lighting essential — procedure light positioned at perineum. If difficulty locating meatus in obese patient: lateral Sims position may help. Female urethra 4cm — catheter only needs to advance 5–6cm before urine flows. Do not inflate balloon until urine drains freely.
